sources.title: rust-peg parameterized grammar rules
sources.sections_read: README features and grammar example
sources.confirmed: rust-peg generates recursive-descent parsers from a Rust macro containing a compact PEG grammar; rules can take arguments and be reused as rule templates.
sources.limits: Moves reuse into a PEG grammar rather than native Rust patterns; grammar semantics and error behavior must be checked when translating an existing parser. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C19.json.

sources.title: combine parser combinators
sources.sections_read: README introduction and combinator example
sources.confirmed: combine composes Rust parsers using operations such as repetition and separation; it uses LL(1) parsing by default with an explicit attempt combinator for lookahead.
sources.limits: Does not add pattern-position syntax; its default LL(1) behavior and opt-in lookahead require checking against the existing parser's recognition behavior. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C19.json.

sources.title: LALRPOP grammar macros
sources.sections_read: README features
sources.confirmed: LALRPOP provides grammar macros for recurring productions, parameterized lists and subsets of productions, alongside grammar-oriented parser generation.
sources.limits: Requires adopting a generator grammar and build workflow; does not itself provide a reusable fragment inside an existing Rust match pattern. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C19.json.

sources.title: GHC pattern synonyms
sources.version_or_date: GHC 9.14.1; homepage dates that release to 2025-12-19
sources.sections_read: PatternSynonyms Since 7.8.1; parameterized pattern examples; unidirectional and bidirectional variants
sources.confirmed: GHC names parameterized pattern schemes independently of representation and supports matching-only and bidirectional forms. The current manual says the extension exists since GHC 7.8.1, but its release date still needs a dated source.
sources.limits: A Rust counterpart needs binding, type and exhaustiveness semantics; the precise 7.8.1 feature set was not checked because its release notes could not be decoded. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C19.json.

sources.title: match.html
sources.version_or_date: Racket 9.3, released August 2026 according to official download page; live manual
sources.sections_read: Extending match: define-match-expander, transformer semantics, expression-context transformer, invocation restriction
sources.confirmed: define-match-expander runs a syntax transformer when its bound identifier heads a pattern and replaces that pattern with the returned pattern; a second transformer can define expression-context behavior. Bare occurrences are bindings, so invocation syntax matters.

sources.version_or_date: Racket 6.0; official version archive dates release to February 2014
sources.sections_read: Pattern grammar and derived patterns; Extending match, define-match-expander transformer semantics and syntax-list example
sources.confirmed: The archived Racket 6.0 manual specifies a transformer that replaces a named pattern at expansion time and optionally gives the same name expression behavior. This directly verifies reusable pattern expansion in a version released before the cutoff.
sources.limits: Requires adaptation to Rust's binding, type and exhaustiveness rules; it is not an importable Rust library. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C19.json.
